## 8. Evidence base carried forward from the checkpoint (re-verified)

1. **Structural template:** `configs/campaigns/p2_015_floors/05_phase_decode_abba/`
   — 40 members, 10 contiguous A/B/B/A blocks, fixed label order, no RNG; generated
   by `configs/campaigns/p2_015_floors/generate_configs.py`, which freezes
   `calibration_plan.json` + `.sha256` and per-stage `order_manifest.json`
   (`joulewise.order_manifest.v1`) and stamps `calibration-plan-sha256=<hex>` into
   every member's tags. Window C executed exactly this shape and passed — the first
   comparative window in project history to pass its whole-window verdict.
2. **Workload shape:** `df_ph_decode` = 128 prompt / 512 output tokens,
   `repetitions: 1`, `warmup_runs: 1`; sampling `power_hz 10.0`,
   `idle_seconds 30.0`, `warmup_seconds 5.0`. The 7B profile is identical except the
   `model` block, so the contrast isolates the model.
3. **Calibration scope literal:** `production_window` is a member of
   `_CALIBRATION_SCOPES` (`joulewise/detection_floor.py:93-98` — the checkpoint said
   93-96).
4. **Condition-family convention:** `joulewise.condition_family_definition.v1`, an
   exact key set validated by
   `joulewise/floor_extraction.py:280-393`; `comparison_policy` and
   `abba_alias_relation` are frozen literals.
5. **Window structure:** `docs/phase_2/window_runbook.md` — pre-calibration + §5B
   screen, in-window NEG-8 bound corpus (12) + bound mint, start triplet (3),
   science, midpoint (1), science, end triplet (3), post-calibration.
6. **Measured member timings** — see §4.

## 9. What changed from the checkpoint

- 7B model: was absent, now downloaded, verified, revision-pinned (§3).
- 7B member duration: was an unmeasured ~120-130 s size-based inference, now a
  ~97 s probe-anchored figure (§4); the budget fell from ~2.9 h to ~2.6 h.
- Disk: the "~13 GB free" concern was stale; 113 GB free (§3).
- Condition family: the checkpoint's single working-name family
  `sw-decode-1p5b-vs-7b` is **wrong-shaped** and is replaced by two per-arm families
  (§10 Q2), because the manifest validator requires
  `floor_selector.condition_family_ids == [condition_a_id, condition_b_id]` and the
  engine partitions evidence per family id before deriving each arm's stack identity.
- Claim consumption: newly discovered to be blocked (§2). This is the material
  change and the reason §5 is conditional.

docs/process_traces/2026-07-17-floor-extraction/extraction-verified.json:65:        "notes": "DERIVATION (docs/phase_2/detection_floor.md §Estimator rule, lines 91-97). Absolute cells: r_i = E_i - mean(E) over strict-valid bundles; floor_abs_j = max(max_i|r_i|, t_{0.975,df=9} * s_r * sqrt(1 + 1/10)) with t_{0.975,9} = 2.2621571628 (table value; scipy unavailable), sqrt(1.1) = 1.0488...; spread_j reported is s_r (sample stddev of residuals = sample stddev of E). Comparative (ABBA) cells: delta_i = (A1+A2)/2 - (B1+B2)/2 within each block; floor_cmp_j = max(max_i|delta_i|, |mean(delta)| + t_{0.975,9} * s_delta * sqrt(1.1)); abba_delta_j reported is mean(delta) across the 10 blocks, spread_j is s_delta. n counts strict-valid bundles (absolute) or strict-valid ABBA blocks (comparative), per the doc's single n definition. n = 10 in every cell, so the 5<=n<10 small-sample guard factor does NOT apply. The output schema has only floor_abs_j, so the two ABBA rows carry floor_cmp_j in that field (labeled in window_class). All values computed from per-bundle summary_metrics.json, cross-checked against campaign_log.jsonl member records, and the mid-gross cell replayed by independent hand arithmetic (exact match).\n\nANOMALIES / CAVEATS: (1) The task said 'per shape cell mid/long' but the campaign executed mid/short: block 08_optional_long_request_absolute has ZERO rows in campaign_log.jsonl — no long-prompt/long-decode request floors exist; short is the second shape actually run, and is what is reported. (2) energy_request_j == idle_subtracted_energy_j exactly (0.0 difference) in all 60 bundles — one idle-subtracted metric under two names; rows are merged accordingly. Gross-vs-idle-sub mid gap (24.0593 - 23.9301 = 0.1293 J) is consistent with idle_mean ~0.119 W times window duration. (3) Claim-readiness anomaly: every one of the 60 bundles has claim_evidence_classification 'flagged', and window_evidence_precheck.gross_request / idle_subtracted_request is eligible=false on ALL 60 — reason clock_bound_exceeds_quarter_window on all (clock_anchor_bound_s ~1.089 s vs 0.25 x window duration ~1.33 s mid / ~0.36 s short), plus cadence_ratio_below_threshold on all 10 short bundles (cadence_ratio ~3.19 < required 4.0). Per §Claim-Gate Thresholds these floors are computable but the underlying request windows currently fail the L2/L3 evidence precheck; P2-037/P2-039 adjudication needed before these floors gate claims. (4) DF-CMP-ABBA-RQ floor_cmp (0.909 J gross) exceeds the absolute floor (0.527 J) — expected per §Comparative Floors; driven by sign-flipping late blocks b07-b10 (deltas +0.457, -0.640, +0.360, -0.535), which look like a drift/ordering pattern in the session tail. (5) All 60 bundles strict_valid=true, status succeeded, collection usable; ABBA block membership complete 4/4 in all 10 blocks. (6) Process note: the codex MCP tool surface was not available in this session (ToolSearch returned no codex tools), so the extraction was done at the lead bench with deterministic scripts instead of a delegated Sol session; every reported number was read directly from bundle artifacts and the headline cell was independently re-derived by hand."

docs/process_traces/2026-07-17-floor-extraction/extraction-verified.json:116:        "notes": "DERIVATION (docs/phase_2/detection_floor.md, false-effect guard floor; n=10 everywhere so no small-sample guard factor): absolute cells use r_i = E_i - mean(E) over strict-valid bundles, floor_abs_j = max(max_i|r_i|, t_{0.975,df=9} * s_r * sqrt(1+1/n)), t_{0.975,9} = 2.2621571628; comparative cells use within-block delta_i = (B1+B2)/2 - (A1+A2)/2 over strict-valid ABBA blocks, floor_cmp_j = max(max_i|delta_i|, |mean(delta)| + t_{0.975,9} * s_delta * sqrt(1+1/n)). The t-prediction term dominated in every cell. SCHEMA MAPPING: for the two DF-CMP-ABBA-PH rows the required floor_abs_j field carries floor_cmp_j (the schema has no separate comparative-floor field); abba_delta_j = mean(delta); spread_j = sample stddev of residuals (absolute rows) or of block deltas (ABBA rows); n counts bundles (absolute) or ABBA blocks (comparative) per the doc's n definition. RESULTING GATES (floor_gate_j = max(floor_abs_j, floor_cmp_j)): prefill 1.738940 J (comparative dominates), decode 1.026892 J (comparative dominates). ANOMALIES: (1) campaign_log.jsonl lists prefill ABBA b01-b05 members twice — executed once 14:00-15:13Z by campaign-20260717T135859310239Z-p31329 (log lines 96-112, status ok), then re-listed status=skipped/exit_code=null at 15:14Z by resumed campaign-20260717T151358798725Z-p33508 (lines 113-129); no double measurement, dedup applied. (2) DF-PH-SHORT-PREFILL is not identifiable (not_resolvable_sample_count on all 10 bundles) — its floor row is smoke evidence only and cannot support L2/L3, matching the cell's designed identifiability-verdict output. (3) Late-campaign decode-ABBA drift regime: idle_window_suspect + drift_term_unknown on all of b06-b10 plus parts of b03/b05, cadence_ratio_below_threshold on b06-b10; both largest-|delta| blocks are flagged, so the decode comparative floor may be drift-inflated (kept, conservative, since all bundles are strict_valid — the doc explicitly allows floor_cmp_j to exceed floor_abs_j under drift/ordering effects). (4) Every DF-PH bundle carries claim-evidence flags cadence_ratio_unrecorded, clock_bound_exceeds_quarter_window, insufficient_in_window_samples — claim-evidence classification 'flagged' throughout; strict_valid inclusion criterion still met for all 110 DF-PH bundles (30 absolute + 80 ABBA), each status=succeeded. Values in Joules, rounded to 6 decimals from full-precision summary_metrics.json fields. Sources: /Users/edr/code/JouleWise/runs/p2_015_floors_window_a/campaign_log.jsonl and per-bundle summary_metrics.json; cell semantics from /Users/edr/code/JouleWise/docs/phase_2/detection_floor.md; block naming from /Users/edr/code/JouleWise/configs/campaigns/p2_015_floors/{02_phase_absolute,04_phase_prefill_abba,05_phase_decode_abba}."

docs/process_traces/2026-07-17-floor-extraction/extraction-verified.json:216:        "notes": "DERIVATIONS. abba_delta_j here is NOT an ABBA contrast: it carries the signed start-to-end reference drift, delta = E_end - E_start (both bundles are identical single-run configs; config.json diff shows only run_id differs — exact scientific condition match confirmed). mean_j = (E_start+E_end)/2; spread_j = sample sd of the two residuals = |delta|/sqrt(2). floor_abs_j follows the detection_floor.md absolute-cell estimator at n=2: max(max|r_i|, t_{0.975,df=1} * s_r * sqrt(1+1/2)) = max(|delta|/2, 12.7062*(|delta|/sqrt2)*sqrt(1.5)) = 11.0038*|delta|. At n=2 this is dominated by t=12.706 and is a drift-anchor diagnostic, NOT a campaign floor; the load-bearing numbers are the deltas. Runs are 9.4 h apart (10:32:44Z vs 19:57:00Z, 2026-07-17). ANOMALIES. (1) Reference drift is large: +31.25% gross, +27.15% idle-subtracted, +34.96% decode-phase, at identical config and identical token counts — end run was slower (window 1.3489 s -> 1.5049 s) and hotter-idling. (2) End bundle idle baseline contaminated: idle_window_suspect=true, idle mean 0.8095 W (sd 0.5832) vs start 0.1241 W (sd 0.0835), gpu_idle_ratio_mean 0.515 vs 0.987 — the gross (+31%) drift is idle-independent and still large, so drift is real, not only baseline artifact. (3) Both NEG-8 bundles have energy_uncertainty_status=not_estimable and window_evidence_precheck gross_request eligible=false (in_window_sample_count 13/15, clock_anchor_bound_s 1.1407/1.1982 s > window/4 of 1.3489/1.5049 s windows, observed sampling ~8.8 Hz). CAMPAIGN QUALITY SWEEP. Tasking said 248 bundles; ACTUAL: campaign_log.jsonl has 248 LINES = 239 run rows + 9 campaign_verdict records, covering 222 distinct bundle dirs; 17 run_ids (df-cmp-abba-ph-prefill b01-a1..b05-a1) appear twice because campaign-20260717T135859Z was interrupted after 17 runs and resumed as campaign-20260717T151358Z, which logged them status=skipped; final verdict for that command is 40 usable. All 222 bundles: strict_valid=true, status succeeded, collection_classification=usable; all 9 campaign_verdict rows verdict=usable with 0 failed/missing/WAIVED (waiver count = 0). However ALL 222/222 bundles carry claim_evidence_classification=flagged (so listing ids individually is the full bundle roster). Per-flag totals (from the 9 final campaign_verdict rows; union-over-all-rows gives identical counts): cadence_ratio_unrecorded 222, clock_bound_exceeds_quarter_window 222, insufficient_in_window_samples 222 (universal trio); cadence_ratio_below_threshold 92; drift_term_unknown 70; idle_window_suspect 69. Flag-set combos: 126 bundles = universal trio only (incl. p2015-neg8-reference-start, rq-mid-abs r01-r10, ph-decode-abs, ph-prefill-abs, abba-rq, most abba-ph-prefill, early abba-ph-decode blocks); 26 = trio + cadence_ratio_below_threshold (rq-short-abs r01-r10, ph-short-prefill-abs r01-r10, abba-su b01/b02 partial); 65 = 6-flag set adding drift_term_unknown + idle_window_suspect (su-sentinel-abs r01-r10, abba-su b03-b10, abba-ph-decode b06-b10 and parts of b03/b05); 4 = trio + drift_term_unknown + idle_window_suspect without below_threshold (abba-ph-decode b03-a1/b03-b2/b05-b2, p2015-neg8-reference-end); 1 = trio + below_threshold + drift_term_unknown (abba-su-b02-a2). Implication: the campaign is collection-complete with zero waivers, but NO bundle currently qualifies as unflagged claim evidence — the universal trio looks systemic (short windows ~1.3-1.5 s vs ~8.8 Hz effective in-window cadence and clock-anchor bound > window/4), a campaign-level condition P2-037/claim gating must adjudicate. Sources: /Users/edr/code/JouleWise/runs/p2_015_floors_window_a/campaign_log.jsonl (flags identical in run rows and verdict rows), per-bundle summary_metrics.json, docs/phase_2/detection_floor.md (estimator), docs/stream_logs/2026-07-17-p2015-floors-prep.md (block 00/11 definitions)."

docs/process_traces/2026-07-17-extension-axes/axes-evaluations.json:107:  "harness_difficulty": "Already covered by the landed surface: SpeculationPolicy draft_model mode + DraftModelIdentity + max_proposed_tokens cap (joulewise/axi_decode_config.py lines 144-249; wired into config normalization/JSON-schema in joulewise/schemas.py lines 572-836); per-emission counter partition and cap enforcement in validate_v2_event (axi_decode_config.py lines 475-508); frozen counter/acceptance-rate rules and reducer 0.6.0 metrics including gross_energy_per_accepted_draft_token_j and burst-size mean/p50/p95/max (docs/specs/axi/sa_burst_decode_contract.md §5, §8.3); AP-SPEC pairing whose only allowed within-pair config differences are the four /speculation/* pointers (§9.2), and the C-023-OUTPUT-IDENTITY exact-token-match gate (§10). New surface needed: (1) an mlx-dspark runtime adapter producing joulewise.events.v2 decode_emission events per verify round — session-scale; per-round accepted counts already exist (mlx-dspark-vendor src/mlx_dspark/generate.py GenResult.accept_lengths/target_forwards/lookup_rounds, lines 25-46), but per-round proposed counts need a small shim in the generate loop; (2) bench-scale provenance pinning: run with lookup_drafts=False (--no-lookup-drafts, cli.py:80/240) and assert lookup_rounds==0, recorded in adapter metadata; (3) per-method on/off campaigns fit today under FAM-AXI-SPEC-DRAFT-MATCHED-OUTPUT, but a DIRECT DSpark-vs-DFlash method contrast is outside the frozen registry (registry_id enum closed to 4 IDs; \"a different ... mechanism ... or contrast set requires a new prospective registry\", §9.2) — that is multi-session/new-subsystem (registry sibling or successor); (4) mlx-dspark's --max-batch continuous batching must be avoided (contract §2.2: continuous is a forbidden enum value requiring a successor). No change to landed schema/validators/reducer is required for the basic per-method measurement.",
docs/process_traces/2026-07-17-extension-axes/axes-evaluations.json:161:  "feasibility": "Mac/MLX today: NOT runnable for native MTP. Grounded locally (stronger than Sol's NEEDS-WEB — Sol missed the repo venv): pinned mlx-lm 0.31.3 at /Users/edr/code/JouleWise/.venv/.../mlx_lm strips MTP weights at load — qwen3_next.py:455 drops all \"mtp.\" keys, mimo_v2_flash.py:364 drops \"model.mtp*\", mimo.py:189 drops \"model.mtp_layers.\" — so MTP-bearing architectures (Qwen3-Next, MiMo) load as plain causal LMs with heads discarded. The same mlx-lm DOES ship external-draft speculative decoding (generate.py:473 speculative_generate_step), and the vendored mlx-dspark clone (/Users/edr/code/mlx-dspark-vendor, verified at 2facf791) implements DSpark+DFlash but has no native-MTP path — so the Mac burst-decode leg is served by external-draft mechanisms today. Whether any newer mlx-lm release or third-party MLX project executes MTP heads at inference: NEEDS-WEB. 3080 Ti (12 GiB): the only named MTP-bearing model that plausibly fits is Xiaomi MiMo-7B quantized (model knowledge, unverified); DeepSeek-V3, Qwen3-Next-80B, and GLM-4.5-class do not fit 12 GiB; vLLM MTP-method support and per-round proposed/accepted counter hooks for the pinned vllm_runtime adapter: NEEDS-WEB. Mac 128 GB fits Qwen3-Next/GLM-Air-class quantized memory-wise, but that is moot without an MLX MTP execution path. AMD/other: outside the D-073 fleet, not evaluated. Note: the concurrently running AXI-SC spike (worktree JouleWise-wt/axi-sc) is probing exactly mlx-lm 0.31.3 spec/MTP observability; my grounding predicts its verdict = external-draft supported, native-MTP unsupported.",
docs/process_traces/2026-07-17-extension-axes/axes-evaluations.json:164:  "summary": "Native MTP is the best-covered and least-runnable of the burst-decode mechanisms: the landed AXI-SA contract already treats it as a first-class speculation mode with its own identity object, registry IDs, family, fixtures, and identical counter semantics to external-draft, so essentially zero new contract surface is needed — but no reachable runtime executes MTP heads today. The decisive grounded fact (which Sol flagged NEEDS-WEB and I resolved at the bench): pinned mlx-lm 0.31.3 in the repo venv strips MTP weights at model load for every MTP-bearing architecture it ships (qwen3_next, mimo, mimo_v2_flash), while fully supporting external-draft speculation — so the Mac leg's characterized burst-decode claims should route to DSpark/DFlash now, with native MTP held as a gated feasibility row. The scientific case for keeping it is real and Q4-shaped: self-drafting removes the external drafter's residency and forwards, making the drafter's fixed-cost term the experimental variable — the cleanest mechanism-level stress of E = fixed + coefficients*work in the whole speculation axis. The C5-2.5 denominator story survives intact under native MTP (proposed = realized candidate positions submitted to verification, never head_count x draft_depth; accepted excludes the bonus token; J/accepted-token stays a spec-on-only mechanism-yield diagnostic with no drafter-energy attribution possible or claimed), with one naming caution: report language should say 'accepted proposal (draft/MTP) token'. Fleet-wise, MiMo-7B is the only named candidate plausibly spanning both legs (model knowledge, unverified); the 12 GiB CUDA cap eliminates DeepSeek-V3/Qwen3-Next/GLM-class. Ranking for the Mac leg: DSpark first, DFlash second, native MTP third as a four-gate spike (heads in source weights, retained through conversion, executed with round counters, exact-output on/off smoke). Enrichment is medium: high distinctness but low near-term askability, and the in-flight AXI-SC spike will supply the authoritative mlx-lm verdict either way."

## Verified doctrine and conflict check

[D-078 clause 11](</Users/edr/code/JouleWise/docs/decision_log.md:4599>) says:

- attribution error is roughly **0.7–1.0 J** per phase member;
- the instrument is attribution-limited rather than noise-limited;
- the practical effective clearable effect is **floor + claim-side bound, approximately 5 J for phase contrasts**;
- workload length is the free lever because the attribution error is approximately duration-independent while the effect scales with workload.

There is no exact **5.000000 J** threshold in the decision log. It is explicitly approximate.

[D-083](</Users/edr/code/JouleWise/docs/decision_log.md:5130>) adds an important wording correction: the expression is not a single summed acceptance gate. The floor gate and claim decision interval are enforced separately; approximately **5 J** remains the correct practical description of what an effect must jointly clear. Thus, if “effective claim bar” in the prompt meant one literal acceptance threshold, the decision log narrows that wording.

D-110 does not void the PASSED windows themselves, but it makes the old minted floors non-claim-bearing because their never-zero allowance was understated. Consequently, old point energies remain usable here as diagnostics; old floor or interval values cannot be promoted.

## Contrast uncertainty composition

For a 7B−1.5B contrast, energy points subtract but uncertainty magnitudes add. D-078’s contrast rule is `Σ|cᵢ|wᵢ`, not root-sum-square.

In the direct ABBA corpus:

- mean 1.5B prefill anchor half-width: **0.768096 J**;
- mean 7B prefill anchor half-width: **1.039955 J**;
- ABBA block-composed contrast half-width: mean **1.808052 J**, range **1.713501–1.908734 J**.

Applying that historical composed half-width to the point delta gives a diagnostic interval of approximately **4.001878–7.617982 J**. Its lower side falls below the practical approximately **5 J** bar. Moreover, D-110 shows that the old minted uncertainty was understated, so these historical widths must not be used to argue for a lower bar.

D-082’s “max, never sum” rule concerns absolute versus comparative components inside one floor cell. It does not authorize RSS or non-composition of the two model measurements in a model contrast.

## Length sensitivity

A purely proportional diagnostic inversion gives nominal break-even at approximately **110 prompt tokens**, which explains why the observed 128-token point estimate is only barely over the practical bar.

Projected from the matched 128-token ABBA delta:

| Prompt length | Projected delta | Point ratio to approximate bar | Interpretation |
|---:|---:|---:|---|
| 128 tokens | 5.809930 J observed | 1.16× | Marginal |
| 192 tokens | 8.714895 J projected | 1.74× | Likely clear, but still extrapolated |
| 256 tokens | 11.619860 J projected | 2.32× | Recommended sizing if the contrast is retained |

The 1.5B clean corpus supports approximate scaling: multiplying its 128-token mean by **32** predicts **52.770445 J**, versus **51.072749 J** observed at 4096 tokens, an approximately **3.3%** difference. That is encouraging, but it is not a substitute for missing long-prompt 7B evidence.

## Rough ABBA arm and runtime

For a retained, lengthened contrast:

- fixed A/B/B/A order;
- ten blocks;
- forty cross-model members total;
- same prompt-token hash across models;
- prospective prompt length of at least 256 tokens;
- `phase_energy_j.prefill` explicitly registered before collection.

The proven 128-token contrast’s forty members took approximately **106.7 minutes** from the first member completion to the last. Window B’s forty-member prefill ABBA took approximately **109.4 minutes**. Thus budget roughly **110 minutes** core, or about **130 minutes** with a 20% member-failure margin.

The proven ten-absolute companion took roughly **25–28 minutes**. A ten-absolute plus forty-null floor design is therefore about **135 minutes** of science-member time before calibrations and references.

Adding a separate forty-member cross-model contrast produces about **245 minutes** of core science-member time before references, calibration, adjudication, and failure margin. That likely exceeds the project’s two-to-four-hour preferred window envelope. If the parent retains the contrast, splitting floor and contrast collection into separate quiet windows is safer than compressing both.

## (iii) Ranked reachable claims — effect/floor arithmetic

Baseline: 7B-4bit decode = 0.376 J/tok, 1.5B = 0.098 J/tok (JouleWise measured). Floor: 6–14 J now, ~2–5 J after tightening. Workload 512–8192 tok.

| Rank | Contrast | Effect estimate | Δ at feasible workload | Effect/floor (14 J) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Weight quant 4b vs 8b (7B) | +60–90% J/tok (bandwidth ∝ bytes) → Δ≈0.22–0.34 J/tok | ×2048 tok ≈ **450–700 J** | **~35–50×** |
| 2 | Spec decode on/off (7B+0.5B) | ±10–30% → Δ≈0.04–0.11 J/tok | ×2048 ≈ **80–230 J** | **~6–16×** |
| 3 | MoE vs dense matched-active | +30–100% of ~0.1–0.15 J/tok dense | ×2048 ≈ **60–300 J** | **~5–20×** |
| 4 | KV-quant 4b vs fp16, long ctx | Qwen2.5-7B KV ≈57 KB/tok fp16 → ~9.6% of decode bandwidth at 8k ctx; save ~75% of it ≈ 3.5% avg over 0→8k | ×8192 ≈ **~100 J** (concentrated late — phase resolution helps) | **~7×** at full 8k; marginal below 4k |
| 5 | Hybrid-linear vs full-attn: J/tok-vs-context slope | GQA slope from KV reads; linear ~flat; tens of % at 16–32k ctx | context-sweep design, per-point Δ ≥ 50–100 J | ~5–10× (**runtime risk**) |
| 6 | MoE top-k slope (same weights) | expert-FFN energy ~∝ k; maybe 20–40% of J/tok | ×2048 ≈ 100–250 J | ~10× (**mechanism knob unverified**) |
| — | MTP | — | — | **unreachable** (no runtime) |

All effect estimates except row 1's bandwidth scaling are extrapolations from server-class literature — flagged as such; that gap is the point.

## (iv) What each claim says that the literature can't

1. **Spec decode**: "On batch-1 unified-memory inference, speculative decoding changes decode energy by X% ± CI" — first *measured* on-device energy verdict incl. the **sign** (all lit is server GPU batch sweeps; mlx overhead could plausibly flip it — issue #250 hints the spec-decode step is slower).
2. **Quantization**: CI-bounded J/token-vs-bits curve on Apple silicon, adjudicating the q4>q8 anomaly the edge literature reports without error bars.
3. **MoE**: whether the +54% matched-active GPU penalty survives unified memory, phase-resolved — direct extension of 2606.21428 (M2 Pro, one pair, coarse) with the sign-flip (matched-active vs matched-total) pinned down on one instrument.
4. **KV quant**: the first measured energy number of any kind — lit has only memory/latency.
5. **Attention slope**: on-device d(J/tok)/d(context) for hybrid-delta vs full attention — 2605.11999 is H200-only and whole-request.

## Top-3 recommended first campaigns

1. **Speculative decoding on/off (Qwen2.5-0.5B→7B, models already characterized)** — cleanest single-mechanism ABBA in existence (identical target weights, flag-toggled), verified runtime, open sign question, 6–16× floor clearance.
2. **Weight-quant ladder (Qwen 7B/8B at 4/8/16-bit)** — 35–50× floor clearance, checkpoints trivially available, and it calibrates the bytes-moved→joules model every other campaign's predictions rest on.
3. **MoE vs dense matched-active (Qwen3-30B-A3B vs Qwen3-4B, plus the OLMoE/OLMo-2 lit-replication pair)** — settles the matched-active vs matched-total sign flip on unified memory and directly extends the only existing Apple-silicon result.

# Calibrated Parameter Scaling on Apple Silicon: Where Phase Energy Becomes Resolvable

**Thesis:** Across five dense Qwen2.5 4-bit models on one M3 Max/MLX stack, decode energy should show a large, resolvable association with parameter count, while short-prefill scaling will expose the instrument’s refusal boundary rather than yield an artificially complete curve.

## Project brief and steps

JouleWise already has the scientific spine of this paper: runtime-defined prefill/decode boundaries, live-bracketed `powermetrics` calibration, attribution intervals, detection floors composed from repeatability, worst-case timing attribution, and never-zero drift, plus hash-bound, fail-closed custody. The instrument is attribution-limited—about 1 J per phase member—and phase contrasts practically need roughly 5 J while separately passing the floor and interval-direction gates. The immediate priority remains the three D-117 windows: 1.5B decode floor with its 128-token prefill rider, 7B decode floor with rider, and the 1.5B-versus-7B decode ABBA contrast. Those windows should produce the two anchor points and the registered broad contrast; historical diagnostics—50.257 J and 192.386 J mean decode energy for 512 tokens, with registered ABBA difference 141.29 J—are sizing evidence only.

To turn those anchors into this paper, add four prospective windows after D-117: separate 0.5B, 3B, and 14B floor windows, each using the proven 10-absolute/40-null design with a prefill rider; then one dual-contrast window containing five ABBA blocks of 0.5B-versus-3B and five blocks of 3B-versus-14B. This produces five phase-energy points and three direct size contrasts spanning the ladder without inventing a five-arm statistical protocol. Total commitment from today is therefore **seven quiet nights: three already required plus four extensions**, approximately 21–23 quiet-machine hours [uncertain, pending 14B timing]. The proposal intentionally stops short of a “scaling law”: [the live registry](</private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-edr-code-JouleWise/58ce57f7-1ee6-4b35-a1b3-457ccf40dff7/scratchpad/desk/docs/research_question_registry.md>) caps 4–6-model studies at descriptive L2 pairwise results unless a larger-model-set ruling is adopted.

## Contributions

1. **Five-point, phase-resolved family characterization.** Report gross prefill and decode joules for Qwen2.5 0.5B/1.5B/3B/7B/14B under independently minted, stack-specific floors; falsified if required cells refuse or measurements do not form the projected ordering.

2. **Three floor-gated parameter-size contrasts.** Test 0.5B→3B, 1.5B→7B, and 3B→14B with ABBA estimators and interval-supported direction; each may independently resolve or refuse.

3. **A floor-aware parameter-forward normalization.** Report  
   `phase J / (runtime-observed phase tokens × published non-embedding parameters)`  
   in pJ per non-embedding-parameter-forward, accompanied by its transformed floor. This is a descriptive normalization—not direct energy attribution or an operation count.

4. **A phase-specific negative result.** Test whether 128-token prefill scaling remains unresolvable even when decode scaling is clear; refusal is the planned result when either gate fails.

## Experiment plan

Qwen publishes this family as dense decoder-only models at the required sizes; published non-embedding counts are approximately 0.36B, 1.31B, 2.77B, 6.53B, and 13.1B. [Qwen2.5 release](https://qwenlm.github.io/blog/qwen2.5/), [3B model information](https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen2.5-3B-Instruct-GGUF), [7B model card](https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct), [14B model card](https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen2.5-14B-Instruct).

A simple line through the two historical decode anchors projects approximately **24, 50, 90, 192, and 371 J** for 512-token decode [highly uncertain extrapolation]. The new registered contrasts would therefore be roughly 66 J for 0.5B→3B and 281 J for 3B→14B, comfortably above 5 J; even ±30% projection error leaves substantial clearance. The historical anchors normalize to roughly **75 pJ** and **58 pJ per non-embedding-parameter-forward** for 1.5B and 7B, suggesting the normalization may decrease with size rather than remain constant—an empirical question, not an efficiency claim.

For 128-token prefill, the same two-anchor projection is approximately **0.6, 1.6, 3.3, 7.6, and 15 J**. Thus 0.5B→3B is projected near 2.7 J and should refuse; D-117’s 1.5B→7B diagnostic is already marginal; 3B→14B projects near 11.7 J and might clear. This mixed outcome is more informative than lengthening prompts until every point succeeds. The optional 256-token arm from the [prefill feasibility study](</private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-edr-code-JouleWise/58ce57f7-1ee6-4b35-a1b3-457ccf40dff7/scratchpad/desk/docs/process_traces/2026-08-07-prefill-feasibility/SYNTHESIS.md>) should remain outside this proposal because its floors do not automatically transport from the 128-token riders.

Desk work comprises artifact acquisition and hash pinning; tokenizer/prompt-token identity audit; 14B load, swap, throughput, and thermal probes; three floor packs; a dual-contrast plan with Holm correction for two new hypotheses; extension of the D-117 multi-cell mint to ten phase cells; parameter-count provenance; normalized-floor propagation; deterministic extraction/figure scripts; and full synthetic refusal regression. Every measured member remains one sequential request, so this **does not violate the frozen single-request boundary**.

## Hardware and instrument

Owned: M3 Max MacBook Pro, 128 GB, `powermetrics`, MLX stack, and local 0.5B/1.5B/7B artifacts. The 3B and 14B MLX 4-bit artifacts are publicly available and approximately 1.74 GB and 8.32 GB respectively. [3B artifact](https://huggingface.co/mlx-community/Qwen2.5-3B-Instruct-4bit), [14B artifact](https://huggingface.co/mlx-community/Qwen2.5-14B-Instruct-4bit). No RTX, Jetson, or new apparatus is needed. **Wall-meter dependency: no**; a borrowed WT310E would strengthen absolute-scale validation but cannot validate phase allocation and should remain the separate C8 axis.

## Venue and relationship to the MVP

This is a strong capstone extension and a good EuroMLSys/HotCarbon or ICPE Emerging paper. By itself it is probably insufficient novelty for ICPE full research because it remains a single-unit, L2 descriptive family study. It could become the empirical evaluation section of an ICPE-full metrology paper alongside artifact evaluation or wall validation.

It reuses the MVP draft’s introduction, measurement boundary, calibration, floor composition, dual gates, fail-closed protocol, and limitations nearly unchanged. New material is the family-selection rationale, parameter normalization, four extension windows, scaling/refusal figures, and multiplicity-controlled pairwise analysis.

## Risks and kill criteria

Kill before spending an extension night if:

- 14B swaps, throttles, or pushes a window beyond four hours with 20% margin;
- artifact audit cannot establish comparable 4-bit/group-size/runtime conditions;
- prompt-token identity or output-policy equivalence fails;
- the mint cannot issue independent phase floors for all five stacks;
- the dual-contrast analysis plan is not frozen and validator-supported;
- desk diagnostics project the smallest registered decode contrast below **10 J**—a conservative 2× sizing buffer.

Any failed floor, contaminated window, or below-bar phase becomes a published refusal, not a substituted model or post-hoc longer workload.

## Relation to Ed’s original goals

This directly serves the **swappable model/size axis** and energy-honest reporting critique. It does not deliver mechanism attribution, MTP, MoE routing, KV innovation, or split inference. Its value is foundational: it establishes how a modular leaderboard should report size-associated energy only when the calibrated instrument can actually distinguish it.
